title: Model rollout stage-drift detection and ops playbook
creator: Ravi Shah
description: After a recent canary rollout we observed 'stage-drift' where request traffic intended for the canary variant intermittently hit the previous stable variant due to a non-atomic route swap combined with delayed version pin reconciliation. This ticket captures detection heuristics, runbook updates, and engineering action items to prevent recurrence and speed recovery.
timeline: 2025-02-10 11:12 UTC - Canary started: variant v2025-02-10-rc1 rolled to 5% using staged routing policy
2025-02-10 11:34 UTC - Spike in trace mismatches: sampled traces show intermittent variant header missing for canary requests
2025-02-10 11:40 UTC - Initial mitigation: manual pin of v2025-01-stable to node pool and rollback of canary to 0%
2025-02-10 12:05 UTC - Full rollback completed, traffic steady but variance noted in autoscaler logs during swap
2025-02-11 09:00 UTC - Postmortem meeting and initial action list drafted
root_causes: Route swap executed as two separate operations (unpublish old -> publish new) leading to transient window where routing table diverged
Autoscaler created temporary compute-backed endpoints during swap which picked up older pinned versions due to delayed version reconciliation
No synthetic or metric-level check for 'stage consistency' (percentage of requests aligning to expected variant) during canary swaps
Rollback gating relied on manual human verification rather than automated invariant checks
postmortem_notes: Stage-drift is distinct from classic misrouting: it is a temporal inconsistency created by non-atomic swap + state reconciliation lag
Customer impact limited to increased latency and occasional unexpected outputs for a subset of requests (no data loss reported)
Existing canary metrics (error-rate, latency) wouldn't have caught this quickly because the issue manifests as variant mismatch rather than traditional SLO deviations
actions: A1: Implement 'stage-consistency' metric and alert - owner: Aisha Patel - due: 2025-02-28
A2: Change route swap to atomic operation in control plane (single transaction or two-phase commit) - owner: Marco Diaz - due: 2025-03-10
A3: Add preflight validation that verifies route->variant mapping in the target cluster before promoting canary beyond 0% - owner: Linh Nguyen - due: 2025-03-05
A4: Build a reconcile-job that detects pinned-version drift and notifies ops + optionally pauses rollout - owner: Diego Romero - due: 2025-03-12
A5: Update runbook with stage-drift playbook and automated rollback gating steps, include exact dashboard panels to check - owner: Emma Johnson - due: 2025-03-01
A6: Create end-to-end test that simulates control-plane interruptions during swap and validates no drift occurs - owner: QA Team - due: 2025-03-20
A7: Instrument canary traffic with immutable trace tokens for sampling exact variant assignment in traces for first 5% of traffic - owner: SRE - due: 2025-02-24
comments: 2025-02-11 Ravi Shah: Drafted initial RCA and action items after postmortem call. We need to prioritize the atomic swap change because other mitigations are compensating controls.

2025-02-18 Marco Diaz: Prototype for atomic swap submitted. Waiting on infra review for migration impact on Dedicated clusters.
2025-02-22 Linh Nguyen: Added preflight checker to canary controller; currently in feature-flagged rollout in staging
2025-02-26 Emma Johnson: Runbook updated with playbook steps and added checklist for on-call during rollouts
